text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today after reporting quarterly earnings on the heels of a steep five-day slide that knocked the stock down 9%. The company released its Q3 results this morning, which appears to have stabilized the decline, though the modest gain suggests investors are still digesting what the report showed amid broader oil sector weakness—crude prices sit at $99.64 per barrel domestically, down sharply from recent weeks.

The larger context is political: Democrats' recent electoral gains mean renewed scrutiny of energy deals and policies, which has weighed on the sector this week. That uncertainty, combined with questions about future oil demand and geopolitical risks flagged by energy executives, has kept a lid on oil stocks despite the earnings announcement.
